pr_title: One corrupt manifest should not wedge model operations
pr_body:
One potential failure mode is an empty file which bubbles up as an EOF error, leading to all attempts to pull anything failing, and listing operations failing.  Instead, continue and warn about the corrupt manifest, and allow re-pulling the model to clean up the corruption.

Fixes #7393 
Fixes #6920
pr_comments:
In an example scenario where llava:7b has a zero length manifest on disk:

At startup the log shows
```
time=2024-11-05T18:31:52.978Z level=WARN source=manifest.go:159 msg="bad manifest" name=registry.ollama.ai/library/llava:7b error=EOF
```

Listing and pulling other models now works and does not show the corrupt model.

Attempting to repull the corrupted model also works:
```
time=2024-11-05T18:31:55.469Z level=WARN source=manifest.go:159 msg="bad manifest" name=registry.ollama.ai/library/llava:7b error=EOF
time=2024-11-05T18:31:55.469Z level=WARN source=images.go:857 msg="pulling model with bad existing manifest" name=llava:7b error=EOF
[GIN] 2024/11/05 - 18:31:56 | 200 |  749.393734ms | 100.126.204.152 | POST     "/api/pull"
```

After which the model shows up in listing operations and runs.

During startup, it will now skip pruning operations to avoid deleting blobs and give the user a chance to re-pull to clear up the corrupt manifest
```
time=2024-11-05T19:32:48.991Z level=WARN source=manifest.go:166 msg="bad manifest" name=registry.ollama.ai/library/llava:7b error=EOF
time=2024-11-05T19:32:48.991Z level=WARN source=routes.go:1214 msg="corrupt manifests detected, skipping prune operation.  Re-pull or delete to clear" error="registry.ollama.ai/library/llava:7b EOF"
```

```
curl -D - https://registry.ollama.ai/v2/library/command-r/manifests/latest
```
server logs would confirm, but this most likely is the same scenario as #7393 and is caused by a corrupt file in the local store which we aren't handling well.

review_comments: Maybe this should be false to avoid removing files in a undefined state?

This gets called in 2 contexts:  PruneLayers, and PullModel.  PruneLayers is already protected and wont be called when there's a corrupt manifest.

PullModel is more nuanced.  deleteUnusedLayers is called with just the layers that are being orphaned by the updated manifest.  I worry that we might make things worse if we stop cleaning up as we pull new manifests.

I'll add a comment explaining the rationale.

Similar to the above thinking - these call sites are more narrowly scoped around layers that were used, but are transitioning to zero ref counts, and I'm a bit concerned one corrupt manifest will result in excessive garbage accumulation when we are more confident we want to remove the given layer.
